subject: DPA: subprocessor carveouts, security questionnaire & eSign path
messages:
From: Samantha King <samantha.king@everledger.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tomás Ruiz <tomas.ruiz@everledger.com>, legal@everledger.com
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Everledger DPA redlines + security questionnaire

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are our initial redlines to Redwood's DPA (Everledger_DPA_Redline_v1.docx) and our completed security questionnaire. A few high-level items from counsel: 

- We need an explicit carveout allowing Everledger to use a specific analytics subprocessor (AnalytixPro) that we already have contracts with; we cannot accept a blanket veto right for approved subprocessors.
- We have a standard flow for customer-provided encryption keys; please confirm Redwood can support BYOK for the dedicated offering or provide an equivalent KMS integration and HSM attestation.
- Cross-border transfer: our privacy team is asking for clarifications on transfer mechanisms for logs and telemetry; can you confirm whether logs contain PII and what retention applies?

For the DPA redline please share counsel's view on the subprocessor notice/change process — our legal prefers a 30-day notice with ability to object to specific new subprocessors on narrow security/privacy grounds, rather than wholesale approval rights.

We would like to close this in R1 if possible. If Redwood can take the carveout and provide a DocuSign path for the clean DPA + annex, we'll circulate for internal approval.

Attaching both files. Happy to hop on a short call with counsel if helpful.

Best,
Samantha King
General Counsel, Everledger
Attachment: Everledger_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (redline)
Attachment: Everledger_Security_Questionnaire_2026.xlsx

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha King <samantha.king@everledger.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 10:24:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Everledger DPA redlines + security questionnaire

Samantha —

Appreciate the thorough redline and the questionnaire. I'm looping in Rishi (privacy counsel) and Laura (commercial ops) to confirm our stance on the subprocessor carveout and BYOK. A few quick notes from my side:

- We can support a targeted carveout for a named subprocessor (AnalytixPro) provided we get a countersigned copy of Everledger's contract with them and confirm their security posture meets Redwood's baseline. We generally avoid permanent carveouts for specific vendors, but are ok with a limited exception documented in the annex.
- For BYOK/KMS: our Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS; for Dedicated customers we offer a KMS integration and can provide attestations. I'll have Rishi confirm the acceptable language.
- Logs: Redwood's standard telemetry does not surface customer prompt/response PII to external ops; audit logs are retained per the commercial retention table. I'll attach the retention table and a short notes doc in follow-up.

Next steps: Rishi and Laura will send a short counsel note by EOD Monday with proposed language we can accept in round 1, and we can put together a clean DPA for eSign if that works for your team.

Connor
Connor O'Brien
Director, Corporate Development | Redwood Inference
Attachment: none

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: FW: Everledger DPA redlines + security questionnaire — privacy counsel notes

Connor / Laura —

Quick counsel note after reviewing Samantha's redline and their security questionnaire: 

1) Subprocessor carveout (AnalytixPro): acceptable as a one-off annex entry. Recommend language: Redwood will list AnalytixPro in Annex II (approved subprocessors) for the term of the agreement; Redwood retains the right to replace or remove any subprocessor that fails to meet Redwood's security baseline, subject to 30 days' notice where practicable. We should not concede an absolute non-removal clause.

2) Notice and objection process: we can accept a 30-day notice window for new subprocessors with an objection right limited to material security or regulatory concerns; objections escalate to counsel and if unresolved allow for termination of the affected services rather than blanket veto. This keeps operational flexibility.

3) BYOK / KMS: confirm in writing: Private and Dedicated support customer-managed KMS; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and a managed KMS. Recommend we add a short statement in Section 6.2 that describes these options and refer to the Security Annex for more details.

4) Logs and retention: Redwood telemetry excludes prompt/response content from external diagnostic streams; audit logs may include hashed identifiers. Recommend adding explicit language: "Diagnostic telemetry does not include end-user prompt or generation content; retention for diagnostic logs is X days unless otherwise agreed." We should not commit to extremely long retention without additional pricing.

5) E-signature path: OK to propose DocuSign. Prepare a clean DPA (Round 1) with the AnalytixPro annex and the BYOK/KMS note; send to Samantha with the DocuSign envelope link.

I'll draft the replacement language and attach a short one-page annex template. Sending now.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Proposed_Annex_AnalytixPro.txt

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha King <samantha.king@everledger.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Everledger DPA redlines + security questionnaire — proposed path for R1 execution

Samantha —

Thanks for the redline and questionnaire. Per our internal review (summary below), Redwood is prepared to accept a limited subprocessor carveout for AnalytixPro documented in an Annex II, and to support BYOK/KMS options as described. We also propose explicit language re: diagnostic telemetry and retention. Please see the key points: 

- Annex II: We will add AnalytixPro as a named subprocessor for the term of the Agreement; Redwood reserves the right to remove or replace the subprocessor for failure to meet Redwood's security baseline. Everledger to provide countersigned AnalytixPro contract or equivalent evidence.
- New subprocessor notice: 30 days' notice for new subprocessors; objection right limited to material security/regulatory concerns, with escalation to counsel and remedial/termination options.
- BYOK/KMS: Confirmed for Private & Dedicated; Hosted customers can use envelope-level encryption. We'll include a short KMS options paragraph in the Security Annex.
- Logs & retention: Diagnostic telemetry does not contain prompt/response content; default diagnostic retention is 90 days unless otherwise agreed.

If this aligns with Everledger's expectations, I've prepared a clean DPA and Annex that we can route via DocuSign for signatures. DocuSign envelope: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/1234-evr-dpa

Proposed next steps:
1) Everledger to confirm acceptance of the Annex wording and provide AnalytixPro contract copy (redlines addressed).
2) Redwood to send DocuSign envelope with clean DPA + Annex for countersignature.
3) Once signed, we will schedule a short onboarding call with ops to configure KMS access.

Happy to discuss by phone — can do 30 minutes tomorrow morning if you'd like.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Director, Corporate Development | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Clean_DPA_R1.docx (to be attached to DocuSign)
